verification.description: Required: 1 to 16 items; [] is rejected. Corrected verification commands. Only after the runtime verification failed and the work itself is fine: it verifies again without redoing the reviewed work. When the code is wrong, submit a new plan instead. Runtime verification runs in one fixed sandbox in every access mode; project writes outside git-ignored directories are discarded when it ends (refused where the host cannot overlay), and no user consent, permission or mode change alters that sandbox, so never ask the user to authorize it. Required for every plan, including an investigation-only or trivial one: verification runs even when nothing changed. The runtime runs these commands once after review, each until it exits; this is where the project's whole documented suite belongs. Copy each command exactly from the project's documented verification (docs/project/verification.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Makefile or package.json scripts), interpreter included, e.g. [["python3","-B","-m","pytest","-q"]]. When the project documents no verification, send the smallest command that exits nonzero if the requested result is wrong, using only the project's files and standard tools, e.g. [["node","--check","src/app.js"]] for a script; for an investigation-only plan, one that checks the investigated files. A command that only prints, reads, lists or searches (echo, cat, ls, grep, rg, find, test, true, read-only git and the like) is refused, because its exit status does not prove the work. Each command is an argv array of literal strings: no shell operators, pipes, redirection or substitution; environment variables as ["env","NAME=value",...]. Availability is probed before accepting the plan. If a tool is missing, arrange project-private installation or another executable approach; if neither is possible, ask the owner immediately through the existing question route.

Literal argument of a verification command, copied exactly from the project's own documented verification (docs/project/verification.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Makefile or package.json scripts) when it documents any, interpreter path included; set environment variables with ["env", "NAME=value", ...]. Runs as argv without a shell: do not use command substitution, backticks, redirection, pipes, shell operators or standalone parentheses. 19a88f0bbaaba52d4dc9eab07a65d4813e9461bf.description: Submit this worker attempt's report, summary and observed checks. A check that failed, was then fixed, and whose later identical rerun passed is `passed`: cite the passing rerun's tool_call_ref and describe the failure-then-fix history in the report. An identical rerun repeats the exact argv and cwd, either on the same operation and profile or across command_run and outside_command in either direction. An explicit supported command_correction can supersede a mistaken invocation with a same-name later passing correction of this attempt, never pass the original argv. Complete whole-worktree git diff --check failures confined to sibling writers' reserved paths are not attributable to this worker; the failed evidence remains visible. Scope diff/whitespace checks to owned paths. `assignment_outcome=failed` is reserved for when the delivered work itself does not reach the assignment's goal, never merely because an earlier attempt failed before being fixed. summary is a short plain-language paragraph -- what was done and the current state -- without internal jargon (runtime codes, route names, revisions, receipts) unless the user asked about them. report is required in every call, a review included, and is one plain string, never an object: the complete report Markdown (optionally titled with report_title), which the runtime publishes; or, after create_draft, draft_write and write_report, only that write_report's report_id. summary, verdict and findings never replace it. Decision-brief items (conclusion, evidence, checks, contradictions, limits, next action) are Markdown sections inside the report, never separate fields. If the engine reports that the call could not be parsed, nothing reached Cortex: resend the same arguments with valid serialization and the same request_key. Use checks=[] only if no automated command ran. Each checks item has name (a stable check name) and outcome (passed|failed|not_run|unverified; there is no status field). passed needs the tool_call_ref, cited by one check only, of a complete exit-0 command_run (or user-confirmed outside_command) of this attempt; failed cites its nonzero receipt; not_run or unverified needs a concrete blocker; command is an optional argv array of strings, descriptive only for passed or failed. Engine-native shell calls, report ids and project_git (context only) are never check receipts. Do not send closed_by; the runtime derives it. Use a fresh request_key for a new result; retry an uncertain call only with the identical key and payload. A review must include verdict=APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK or INCOMPLETE (INCOMPLETE with not_covered, each item with its blocker). Every predecessor report in the review packet is read to its last page, and every changed file the packet marks required (this task's own changes; the other listed files are context only) is read completely, unless an INCOMPLETE review names it in not_covered with its blocker; otherwise the submission is refused with review_predecessor_reports_required or review_file_coverage_required, listing what is outstanding in missing. An open failed check is otherwise refused with open_failed_check before recording or publishing (a review whose verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK or INCOMPLETE may cite a failed check as evidence for it: that review is recorded as completed and its verdict routes the task; only APPROVE cannot carry an open failed check), leaving the channel active; the refusal names the failed receipt, the relevant rerun and its evidence gap, and says when no exact rerun can close it. A failed receipt that any result_submit of this attempt already presented (even a refused one) must be cited again by every later submission, failed outcome included, or it is refused with omitted_failed_check. A mistake in your own bounded standalone python/python3 -c probe (a syntax error, one wrong regex literal or one wrong literal-data expectation) may instead be retracted with checks[].invocation_error bound to the corrected passing run: both receipts stay visible and the failure is retracted, not passed. Runtime verification and actual project test/lint/build failures are never retracted. A mistyped command line whose own output shows the check never started (usage, unrecognized-flag or file-not-found error for the command itself) is not a failed check: do not cite it; cite the corrected command's receipt and describe the mistyped run in the report. The receipt carries node_status (completed or failed), not task acceptance. Unknown fields such as artifacts (which belongs to write_report) are rejected. Finish the assignment before submitting: a refusal that names outstanding items (in missing) leaves this assignment active in the same session; complete them and submit again.

inputSchema.description: Structured fields; use the exact advertised properties.

assignment_outcome.description: Optional: send failed only to intentionally submit a failed assignment, when the delivered work itself does not reach the assignment's goal -- never merely because a check failed before being fixed. Otherwise an open failed check is refused with open_failed_check before recording or revoking the channel; rerun exactly the receipt argv at the same cwd (on the same operation, or across command_run and outside_command) and cite the later passed receipt. Never silently omit a real failed check (a mistyped command line that never started the check is not one; see checks[].outcome). Even with failed, every failed receipt an earlier result_submit of this attempt presented must be cited again, or the result is refused with omitted_failed_check. It requires blocker naming the dead end; without one it is refused with assignment_blocker_required.

blocker.description: Required with assignment_outcome failed, ignored otherwise: the dead end that stops this assignment and that you cannot clear yourself within your role and permissions. Finish everything you still can first. A failed submission without a valid blocker is refused with assignment_blocker_required and the assignment stays active in this session. A recorded blocker goes to the coordinator, which clears it, consults the senior consultant or asks the owner according to the task's run mode.

detail.description: The concrete obstacle in plain words: exactly which access, decision, other role's work or tool is needed, and what you already tried.

kind.description: Dead-end category: missing_access (the work needs access or a permission your role does not have and cannot obtain through an access route it is offered), owner_decision (a decision only the owner can make; when ask_question is offered, ask it first and continue with the answer), other_role_work (work another role must do first, such as a change a read-only role may not make), or tool_unavailable (a tool or host capability the work needs is unavailable). Lack of time, effort or attention is never a dead end.

checks.description: Declare planned automated checks early through check_preflight before work depends on them. A missing executable must be installed project-privately or replaced with an executable approach; if neither is possible, ask the owner immediately. Qualitative human-only judgements are separate manual items: report them with no command and a concrete blocker; Workspace labels them Check manually, never a pass/fail or acceptance blocker. Policy-prohibited checks remain explicitly not_run with their named policy, never failed or automatically executed. Automated command checks, up to 20; [] when no command ran and no check was blocked. Each item needs name and outcome (passed, failed, not_run, unverified). A passed check needs tool_call_ref copied from an exit-0 command_run or confirmed outside_command of this attempt; command argv alone never verifies it. A failed check may cite its nonzero receipt. not_run or unverified require a concrete blocker; command argv is retained only for these gap checks and may identify the exact blocked command. A supplied command on passed/failed is ignored as evidence; the runtime derives the command from the receipt. Do not send closed_by: the runtime calculates it. project_git is context only, not a check receipt: describe its status/diff observations in the report, never cite or invent a receipt from large_output_id. These are not qualitative review remarks: read files and inspected code belong in the report body, not checks.

items.description: Structured fields; use the exact advertised properties.

blocker.description: Required and non-whitespace for not_run and unverified; forbidden for passed and failed. State the concrete condition that prevented running or establishing this specific check: for example, a named unavailable host, or a documented project policy that requires an explicit owner request which was not given, such as "paid live check not requested by the owner". "Not run", "out of scope" or "not requested" alone is not a blocker.

command.description: Required: 1 to 128 items; [] is rejected. Optional literal argv. This command is retained only for not_run or unverified gap checks; it identifies the blocked command and lets a later verified identical run close the gap. For passed or failed, it is descriptive only: the runtime derives the actual command and pass/fail evidence exclusively from tool_call_ref, never from this array.

items.description: One literal argument of the command this check ran or would run.

command_correction.description: Optional explicit supersession of a failed invocation by a corrected command; retain both checks. Runtime derives superseded_by, never send it.

corrected_by.description: Exact tool_call_ref of the later verified passing correction, cited once with the same check name in this result and same attempt, operation, cwd and profile, with different argv. Never a runtime verification receipt.

reason.description: Explain the command mistake and correction. Eligible: supported standalone Python probe syntax/regex/literal-expectation corrections, or a direct Python script whose complete output contains only argparse usage and an unrecognized-arguments or missing-required-arguments startup error (exit 2), corrected without changing script/interpreter flags. Real project test/lint/build failures cannot be superseded by another argv. Both receipts stay visible; the failure stays failed history with runtime-derived superseded_by, current outcome superseded, never passed.

invocation_error.description: Optional explicit self-retraction on a failed check only. Bind a supported invocation error to a later passing correction and explain it; runtime validates both receipts and retains the failure, not a synthetic pass. Do not send retracted_by or closed_by.

corrected_by.description: Exact tool_call_ref of a later observed passing correction, cited once as a passed check with the same name in this result and same attempt, operation, cwd and profile; only the -c probe source may differ, and it must differ. Never a claimed, foreign, incomplete, trivial or runtime-owned verification receipt.

reason.description: Nonempty explanation of your own probe invocation mistake and its correction. Eligible only: a failed bounded standalone python/python3 -c probe (only -B, -I or -S before -c) with complete retained output that hit a source-backed SyntaxError; a regex/AssertionError over a literal re pattern; or an AssertionError in a literal-data probe (only single-assignment literal bindings and == asserts, with unary len/sorted/sum/min/max/all/any/abs) whose expectation is statically false. The correction changes exactly one regex pattern literal, or the one false expected literal so every assertion holds; nothing else may change. Runtime verification and actual project test/lint/build failures cannot be retracted. The failed outcome and receipt stay in history with runtime-derived retracted_by; current outcome is retracted, never passed. Other invocation errors retain the existing mistyped-command or exact-rerun path.

name.description: Specific stable name of this automated command check, e.g. "unit tests for services/trading" or "ruff on changed files". Reuse exactly the same name for a later passing rerun that closes this check; do not use a report title, task name, or qualitative review remark.

outcome.description: passed: you ran it in this attempt with command_run (or a user-confirmed outside_command) and it exited 0; requires tool_call_ref (see its evidence rule). failed: it ran and failed; always kept as failed, and result_submit refuses an open failure with open_failed_check unless assignment_outcome="failed" intentionally submits a failed assignment. A failure closes only when a later passed check of this same result cites a rerun of exactly the same command -- the same argv and cwd, on the same operation and profile or across command_run and outside_command in either direction -- that is the latest such run in this attempt: then it stays as history with closed_by. Report a fixed failure that way, or cite only the passing rerun and describe the failure-then-fix history in the report, never by silently dropping it; a different argv needs an explicit supported command_correction (superseded history, never a pass of the original argv). A direct whole-worktree git diff --check whose complete whitespace diagnostics name only sibling writers' reserved paths is runtime-attributed not_attributable, never passed; own writes, unknown paths and runtime verification remain failures. A supported mistake in your own bounded standalone Python probe (see invocation_error.reason) may instead be explicitly retracted with invocation_error; it remains failed history with retracted_by, never passed. 389d5bd87e0afcd82f2e662b93f3235e3dc5b4cf.description: Run one brokered command (argv, no implicit shell) as the owner. Writing workers in Development or Auto get host-writable mounts, an outside cwd and ordinary host resources without routine approval; in Guarded, and for read-only roles in every mode, the host is read-only except tool caches and temp, and writes stay in the granted project scope. Read-only/Guarded commands use private scratch at /var/tmp, not the host directory; a missing path there does not prove host absence. For authorized host-only reads, use an offered outside_command with consent before executing, not a guessed mount or a retry after permission refusal. Read-only investigators cannot use that route: report the capability gap for runtime replanning to a suitable writing specialist, without broadening the requested read. Deletion commands recognized from the argv text (rm, unlink, rmdir, shred -u, find -delete, git clean/rm, rsync --delete, also through common wrappers and sh -c) require consent (Auto answers it itself) and are refused to read-only roles; a deletion inside a script, interpreter or build tool is not recognized. Docker and arbitrary code can bypass direct masks; capability never authorizes hazardous or production actions. Returns argv, exit_code, a tool_call_ref (the evidence a passed result_submit check must cite), output inline up to 64 KiB with output_truncated and the full byte_count, and large_output_id: the complete output is always retained, verifies checks whatever its size and pages with read_large_output, so never redirect or truncate a check's output yourself. A writing worker's command that needs the host is rerun by the runtime itself through outside_command's consent route (Auto answers it itself) and that receipt is returned with rerouted naming why: sudo, pkexec or doas in the argv (before any sandboxed run), a sandbox that could not be prepared, or a run that failed because the host refused a nested sandbox or root inside the sandbox. Read-only roles are never rerouted. Not available to coordinators or consultants. Long commands return running with tool_call_ref. Use command_status on this channel until settled.

Such a script verifies a result_submit check only as setup commands (umask, export, cd, set) joined by ; or && and then one simple check command, for example ["bash","-c","umask 022 && cargo test"]. Only scoped workers may run commands. Read-only/Guarded commands have private scratch /var/tmp; FileNotFoundError there is not proof of host absence.
